title: Softsign: Smooth Sign in Your Optimizer For Better Parameter Heterogeneity Handling
claim: A smooth temperature-controlled transform bridges hard-saturating and linear-clipped update maps, staying linear near zero yet approaching sign for large temperature.
layout: single line plot, four overlaid curves, legend top-left, shared x-axis
description: A single function plot with the input gradient g^k on the x-axis from -2 to 2 and the update value on the y-axis from -1 to 1, on a light grid. A legend in the upper left names four curves. A light-blue dashed step function is the hard sign map, jumping from -1 to 1 at zero. A pink solid line is clip, linear between -1 and 1 and flat outside. A dark-blue solid curve, tanh(t g^k) with t tending to infinity, is a very steep sigmoid that nearly coincides with sign. A magenta dashed curve, tanh(g^k), is a gentle S-shape that tracks clip near the origin and saturates smoothly. The eye goes to the steep blue curve and the sign step at the center, then to the contrast with the gentler curves.
caption: Comparison of update transformations. The hard sign map produces constant-magnitude updates for all non-zero inputs, while clipping preserves linear behaviour only near the origin and saturates outside a fixed threshold. The temperaturecontrolled soft-sign map tanh(τx) smoothly interpolates between these regimes: or large τ it approaches sign(x), whereas around the origin it remains linear.
abstract: Sign-based and LMO-inspired optimizers have recently attracted substantial attention in deep learning due to their strong performance and low memory footprint. However, their fixed-magnitude updates can hurt terminal convergence: they decouple update mechanisms from gradient magnitudes and fail to account for parameter heterogeneity, often leading to oscillation rather than convergence. We propose SoftSignum, a smooth relaxation of sign-based optimization that replaces the hard sign map with a temperature-controlled soft-sign transformation, enabling a parameter-wise transition from sign-like updates to magnitude-sensitive SGD-like steps. We complement it with an adaptive quantile-based temperature schedule and extend the same principle to matrix-valued optimizers, obtaining SoftMuon. We also develop a generalized geometry-relaxation framework based on strongly convex regularizers and Fenchel conjugates, proving convergence in stochastic non-convex setting. Experiments on diverse deep learning tasks, including LLM pretraining, show that SoftSignum and SoftMuon consistently improve over their hard sign-based counterparts and standard AdamW.
